title: Rhubarb frangipane tart
subtitle: spring rhubarb tart with almond frangipane filling
excerpt: A rhubarb frangipane tart sets a layer of almond frangipane in a blind-baked pastry case, then bakes rhubarb lengths into the surface. The frangipane puffs up and sets around the rhubarb, which softens and colours beautifully. The sharpness of the rhubarb against the buttery almond filling makes this one of the most naturally balanced fruit tarts.
sourceNotes: Frangipane, a sweet almond cream used as a tart filling, appears in French pâtisserie from at least the 16th century, reportedly named after the Marquis Frangipani. Its use as a tart base that supports a fruit layer on top is a standard technique in British and French baking alike, used with plums, pears, cherries, and figs as well as rhubarb. Forced rhubarb (grown in the dark to produce pale pink, tender stems) appears in January; outdoor rhubarb follows from April. Both work in this tart, though forced rhubarb produces a more vivid pink colour.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best eaten on the day; the pastry softens overnight. The frangipane can be made 1 day ahead.
recipe.temperatureNote: for the frangipane fill; blind bake the case first at 190°C

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: 180°C conventional (160°C fan) for the frangipane; 190°C for the blind bake

content.text: Rhubarb frangipane tart puts tart rhubarb against rich almond filling, one of the most natural fruit and pastry pairings. The frangipane is spread into the blind-baked case, rhubarb is pressed into the surface, and the whole thing bakes together. The rhubarb sinks slightly as the frangipane rises around it.

items.prepNote: trimmed and cut into 8 cm lengths

content.text: Make, chill, and blind bake the pastry

Rub the butter into the flour and icing sugar until like fine breadcrumbs. Add the egg yolk and cold water, bring together into a dough, wrap and refrigerate 30 minutes. Roll to 3 mm, line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin, and refrigerate 20 minutes more. Blind bake at 190°C for 15 minutes with baking beans, then 8 minutes more without until the base is dry. Leave to cool slightly before filling.

Preheat the oven to 180°C conventional (160°C fan). Beat the softened butter and 120 g caster sugar together until pale. Add the eggs one at a time. Fold in the ground almonds and 2 tablespoons of flour. Spread the frangipane evenly in the pastry case. Arrange the rhubarb lengths across the surface, pressing them gently in. Sprinkle with the remaining 2 tablespoons of caster sugar. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the frangipane is set, puffed, and light golden. Cool on a wire rack for 20 minutes before serving.
